round_3_findings_addressed.finding: 1 (High) -- interpreter selection violates the repair contract: scripts/lib/pick_python.sh accepted any executable .venv-noam/bin/python without the import probe, even when a later PATH candidate was valid.
round_3_findings_addressed.resolution: noam_pick_python now applies the same `import pydantic, yaml` probe to the declared environment: `if [[ -x "$declared" ]] && _noam_python_has_deps "$declared"`. A broken declared environment is skipped deterministically and selection continues to $NOAM_PYTHON then the fixed PATH candidate list; the all-candidates-unavailable path still prints the shared actionable multi-line error via noam_require_python and returns 1. The library header comment was updated to describe probing the declared environment (the round-2 comment claimed it was deliberately unprobed). New negative tests in tests/noam_core/test_interpreter_selection.py: test_broken_declared_environment_falls_through_to_path (broken .venv-noam + usable python3 on PATH -> python3 selected) and test_broken_declared_environment_and_no_usable_path_fails (broken .venv-noam + no usable PATH interpreter -> exit 1, actionable error mentioning pydantic). The existing test_declared_project_environment_wins (declared env has deps -> selected) still passes, so precedence of a *working* declared env is preserved.

round_3_findings_addressed.finding: 2 (High) -- the declared generated environment is not fully ignored: .gitignore had no .venv-noam/ rule, so pyvenv.cfg and lib/site-packages remained candidate files.
round_3_findings_addressed.resolution: Added a narrow `.venv-noam/` directory rule in .gitignore immediately after `.venv/`, with a comment noting the generic `bin/` rule only covered its bin/. The rule is placed well above the `.agents/` sentinel/negation block and shares no path prefix with it, so the three durable reviewer records (.agents/tasks/, .agents/handoffs/, .agents/review-log.md) remain re-included and the two ephemeral dotfiles remain ignored -- unchanged from round 2. NOTE: `git check-ignore -v` could NOT be run in this sandbox (git aborts because it cannot read /Users/apple/.gitconfig, which is outside the sandbox's allowed read scope, and HOME/GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL overrides for git are blocked by the non-interactive permission policy; this matches the recorded round-2 limitation). The reviewer must confirm outside the sandbox that a representative .venv-noam/ root path, .venv-noam/pyvenv.cfg, a .venv-noam/lib/.../site-packages file, and .venv-noam/bin/python are all ignored, while .agents/tasks/TASK-001-phase-a-closure.md, .agents/handoffs/TASK-001-phase-a-closure.json, and .agents/review-log.md are NOT ignored and .agents/.last-review-hash / .agents/.review-round-count ARE.

round_3_findings_addressed.finding: 3 (High) -- domain-scoped references can cross domains silently: src/noam/registry/validate.py checked only global id existence, so a Maxwell Study/Experiment/Result could reference a Joule Capability and a Maxwell Study a Joule Precedent while validation reported success.
round_3_findings_addressed.resolution: Global id uniqueness and the domain-directory containment check (_check_domain_matches_dir) are retained unchanged. Added: capability_domain / precedent_domain maps (id -> declared domain string) built from the same loaded records; a helper _check_reference_domain(ref_id, ref_domain, study_domain, where, kind) that returns a problem when the target domain differs from the containing study's domain (a target with no declared domain is also reported as a mismatch, but Capability/Precedent both require `domain`). Wired into: study.capability_ids, study.precedent_ids, experiment.capability_ids, and result.capability_id -- each only after the id is confirmed to exist. For result.capability_id the check runs before the existing 'capability not among its experiment's capability_ids' check and short-circuits it (a cross-domain reference is the more fundamental fault). Negative tests added to tests/noam_core/test_registry.py: test_detects_study_capability_reference_crossing_domain, test_detects_study_precedent_reference_crossing_domain, test_detects_experiment_capability_reference_crossing_domain, test_detects_result_capability_reference_crossing_domain (all Maxwell study -> Joule target). Same-domain passing fixture: test_same_domain_capability_and_precedent_references_are_valid (Maxwell study wired to a Maxwell capability + Maxwell precedent through experiment and result -> report.ok). Real studies/S001_airport_cw (Maxwell, no capabilities/precedents) still validates with no problems.

round_3_findings_addressed.finding: 4 (High) -- malformed authoring YAML escapes structured validation: _load_all and the study.yaml load caught only pydantic ValidationError, so a PyYAML parse failure propagated through cmd_registry_validate as a traceback.
round_3_findings_addressed.resolution: validate.py now imports `yaml` and both load sites catch `(ValidationError, yaml.YAMLError)`, appending a path-specific problem string and continuing the scan over the remaining files. yaml.YAMLError is the base class of PyYAML's ScannerError/ParserError, so flow/scanner faults are covered. cmd_registry_validate already returns 1 (non-zero, no traceback) whenever report.problems is non-empty, so the CLI contract is satisfied without further change. Tests added to tests/noam_core/test_registry.py: test_malformed_study_yaml_is_reported_not_raised (broken study.yaml -> validate_registry() returns a report, does not raise, problem names study.yaml) and test_malformed_child_yaml_is_reported_and_scan_continues (broken requirements/REQ-001.yaml plus a separately-broken insight -> both problems reported, proving the scan continued past the parse failure).

yaml.YAMLError is the correct base class to catch for all PyYAML parse failures raised by yaml.safe_load in noam.utils.yaml_io.load_yaml (ScannerError, ParserError, ComposerError, ConstructorError all subclass it).

A domain-scoped reference whose target record declares no `domain` at all should be treated as a mismatch; in practice Capability and Precedent both make `domain` mandatory, so this branch is defensive only.
The two ephemeral .agents dotfiles remain the only non-durable files under .agents/; tasks/, handoffs/, review-log.md stay tracked (unchanged from round 2).
limitations: `git check-ignore` could not be executed here. Finding 2's fix is reasoned against gitignore(5): `.venv-noam/` is an early, self-contained directory rule that shares no path prefix with the later `.agents/` sentinel/negation block, so it cannot affect the durable-record re-inclusion, and it ignores the whole generated tree (root, pyvenv.cfg, lib/site-packages, bin/). Independent confirmation outside the sandbox is required before integration.

The external Stop-hook (~/.claude/scripts/codex-review.sh) still enforces its own MAX_ROUNDS=2 and still re-appends a bare `.agents/` line if the literal string `.agents/` is absent from .gitignore. The sentinel line is unchanged and still exactly `.agents/`, so the hook's `grep -qx '.agents/'` should still match and not append a duplicate. If a second un-negated bare `.agents/` line ever appears at end-of-file it must be removed before any commit, because as the last-matching pattern it would re-ignore the durable records.

Cross-domain enforcement compares the target's declared domain against the containing Study's `domain`. A future multi-domain study (none exists) would need this relaxed to a set membership check; that is out of scope for this gate.
Study.capability_ids / precedent_ids are validated for existence and domain, not for 'the study actually exercises this capability'. Unchanged from round 2; out of scope.
No live `codex` review has been obtained for this handoff; it is submitted for that independent review, not a record of one already passed.
unresolved_risks: If the Stop-hook appends a second, un-negated bare `.agents/` line at end-of-file, that trailing line would re-ignore the whole directory as the last matching pattern. The reviewer/integrator should inspect the tail of .gitignore immediately before creating the baseline commit.

pick_python.sh's candidate list is fixed; a site whose only usable interpreter is named outside that list and outside .venv-noam / $NOAM_PYTHON still fails loudly. That is the intended failure mode; $NOAM_PYTHON is the supported escape hatch and should be documented in README.md in a later docs pass.

The malformed-YAML handling reports the raw PyYAML exception text in the problem string. It is path-prefixed and single-record-scoped, but a very large malformed file would produce a long message; acceptable for a local hand-edited registry.
